proof:
In any bounded parameter neighborhood let $T_z$ bound the absolute thresholds of the frame caps at $z$. Their maximum margin is at least $\|x\|_\infty-T_z$. Comparing with the maximum margin at $x=0$ gives existence of a minimizer and a common bound on all minimizers throughout a sufficiently small neighborhood of any parameter. Thus the minimax value can be computed on a fixed larger cube with every minimizer in its interior. The value is locally Lipschitz by uniform Lipschitz bounds for all margins on that cube before taking the maximum and minimum. For $G=\max(0,\max_z(-F_z))$, reducing every offset by $G$ increases all margins and each $F_z$ by $G$, repairs coverage, and has parameter distance $\sqrt m G$. The repair remains in the parameter manifold because all offsets are free.

For a fixed source polytope, all cap volumes and first moments are semialgebraic functions of the parameters. The possible vertices of the clipped polytope solve finitely many square systems in the coefficients. Partition by nonvanishing determinants, feasibility, incidences and the determinant signs in a pulling triangulation; vertex coordinates on each piece are rational, and the simplex determinant and simplex centroid formulas then give piecewise rational volumes and first moments, with zero contributions from lower-dimensional clips. The hinge is a linear combination of those moments and masses with affine-parameter coefficients. Coverage is semialgebraic by the quantified balanced certificate in the attainment theorem. Existence of a feasible parameter with a given objective and absence of any better feasible parameter are first-order real conditions, so Tarski–Seidenberg gives semialgebraicity of the attained value graph. The feasible domain is upward closed and the value is nonincreasing. One-variable semialgebraic $C^1$ decomposition gives the finite exceptional set in its interior.

The hinge is continuously differentiable by dominated differentiation, since the cap plane has zero source $d$-volume, with cap gradient $(Z_i,X_i,-c_i)$ in $(a_i,u_i,b_i)$. The cap mass is locally Lipschitz by bounding its membership change in each bounded fiber by a slab of thickness proportional to the parameter change. Use the proper-section and common-density gradient argument of accepted fact c343c9f3dc96957e. In particular, the support-cut exceptional graphs remain null in either cap's actual parameter chart because $b_i$ is free. Away from those graphs the ambient derivative exists and its restriction is the chart derivative. Taking nearby ordinary gradients away from the null set and projecting their sections as in the accepted proof gives a common-density ambient Clarke gradient that pulls back to the selected chart gradient. This applies to the fixed frame normals as well as the free normal charts; no claim is needed that arbitrary section densities give gradients.

For clarity, the Clarke gradient inclusion for coverage follows directly from the compact cube. Let $f(p,x,\lambda)=\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(z,x)$ where $p$ denotes the local parameters. On the cube use finite convex minimax with simplex weights $\lambda$, and let $x_0$ be a primal optimum at $p$. For a nearby $p'$ and an optimal dual $\lambda'$ at $p'$, the saddle inequalities give
$$
F_z(p')-F_z(p)\le f(p',x_0,\lambda')-f(p,x_0,\lambda').
$$
Along a ray in any chart direction every cluster point of $\lambda'$ is dual optimal at $p$ by compactness and continuity of the weighted minima. Hence at a differentiability point the gradient in every direction is bounded above by the largest pairing with a feature $\lambda_i(z,x,-1)$ of a saddle pair, pulled back to the chart. By separation the ordinary gradient lies in their convex hull. The compact saddle graph is closed locally, so by taking limits and convexifying, the same inclusion holds for Clarke gradients. Finite-dimensional Carathéodory yields a finitely supported probability measure for each selected feature combination. Every primal optimum is strictly inside the chosen cube. Therefore every optimal dual weighted affine function has zero continuous normal, because that primal optimum minimizes it on the cube. At $F_z=0$ the maximum margin there is zero and its weighted average is zero, giving the stated signs and zero weighted individual margins. In particular the pairs are also saddle pairs of the unrestricted LP.

Fix a minimizer $p_*$ at a regular interior budget and write $s(p)=\max_i c_i(p)/M$. If $s(p_*)=\tau$, then $f_0(p)=\Psi(p)-w(s(p))$ is well-defined and locally Lipschitz near $p_*$, since $w$ is $C^1$ near $\tau$ within its feasible domain. It is nonnegative on nearby whole-space covers and vanishes at $p_*$. The offset repair therefore makes $f_0+B\sqrt m G$ have a local unconstrained minimum on the parameter manifold for a local Lipschitz constant $B$ of $f_0$. Indeed, its value at $p$ is at least $f_0$ at the repaired cover. Clarke's Fermat, sum, chain and maximum inclusions yield stationarity with objective coefficient one. The budget contribution uses a convex combination of the gradients of the active caps, with coefficient $-w'(\tau)/M\ge0$, giving exactly $M\sum_i r_i=-w'(\tau)$. The coverage contribution is a nonnegative combination of negative gradients of the active $F_z$, coming from the maximum with zero in $G$. If instead $s(p_*)<\tau$, monotonicity and feasibility of $p_*$ at nearby lower budgets imply $w'(\tau)=0$. Near $p_*$ all covers satisfy the budget, so the same repair applied to $\Psi$ yields stationarity with every $r_i=0$.

The free offset and tilt stationarity equations give the stated mass and base-moment equations for all caps. For a variable unit normal the continuous stationarity vector is parallel to $u_i$. Its dot product with $u_i$ is $\Psi_i$ by using the mass and tilt equations and the identities
$$
u_i\cdot X_i+a_i\cdot Z_i-b_i c_i=\Psi_i,\qquad
u_i\cdot X_i^s+a_i\cdot Z_i^s-b_i S_i=0,
$$
together with the zero margin at positively weighted contacts. This proves the continuous equation on its asserted blocks. Sum the mass and base equations, with factors $u_i$ for the two vector or matrix force identities, and use $\sum_i\lambda_i u_i=0$ and $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$. Finally, the sum of the tilt equations paired with $a_i$ minus the mass equations multiplied by $b_i$ gives zero: for each active pair $\sum_i\lambda_i(a_i\cdot z-b_i)=\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(z,x)-x\cdot\sum_i\lambda_i u_i=0$. Using the cap and section identities in this sum gives the scalar formula for $w$. This last step uses the free offset and tilt equations for the frame, so it requires no frame-normal stationarity.

statement:
Take the framed whole-space cover problem above with $m=N+2d$ caps, the $N$ variable normals constrained to the unit sphere and the $2d$ frame normals fixed at $+e_l,-e_l$. All offsets and base tilts are free, and the full-dimensional source fibers are polytopes. Let $w(\tau)$ be the attained minimum total hinge at budget $c_i\le\tau M$. Its feasible domain is upward closed. On the interior of its feasible domain the value is $C^1$ except at finitely many budgets. At every budget in the remaining interior and for every minimizer, there is normal stationarity with objective multiplier one and nonnegative multipliers $r_i,\eta_z$ satisfying
$$
r_i(c_i-\tau M)=0,\qquad \eta_zF_z=0,\qquad M\sum_i r_i=-w'(\tau).
$$
For each cap, write $Z_i,X_i$ for the first moments of its source mass in $z,x$. Write $S_i,Z_i^s,X_i^s$ for consistent mass and first moments on its source sections $K_z\cap\{L_i(z,\cdot)=0\}$, with $\mathcal H_{d-1}$ density in $[0,1]$, equal to one almost everywhere on proper sections, and such that $(Z_i^s,X_i^s,-S_i)$ is a consistent Clarke cap-mass gradient in full affine cap parameters. For each active fiber margin with positive $\eta_z$ use a finitely supported probability measure $\nu_z$ on optimal whole-space LP saddle pairs $(x,\lambda)$, with $p_{zi}=\int\lambda_i\,d\nu_z$ and $q_{zi}=\int\lambda_i x\,d\nu_z$. Each pair satisfies $\sum_i\lambda_i u_i=0$, $L_i(z,x)\le0$, $\lambda_i L_i(z,x)=0$; the point $x$ is in $\mathbb R^d$. With terms of zero multiplier omitted, for every cap
$$
W_i:=c_i+r_i S_i=\sum_z\eta_z p_{zi},\qquad
Z_i+r_i Z_i^s=\sum_z\eta_z z p_{zi},
$$
and for each variable-normal cap
$$
X_i+r_i X_i^s-\sum_z\eta_z q_{zi}=\Psi_i u_i.
$$
In particular, with all sums running over both types of cap,
$$
\sum_i W_i u_i=0,\qquad
\sum_i u_i(Z_i+r_i Z_i^s)^T=0,\qquad
\sum_i W_i=\sum_z\eta_z,\qquad
w(\tau)=\sum_i u_i\cdot(X_i+r_iX_i^s).
$$
title: Normal stress at regular budgets for framed whole-space hinge covers
